rationale: The workflow installs Python dependencies (pip install . and pip install .[dev]) for every matrix Python version on every run, with no dependency cache. The repository provides pyproject.toml as a stable cache input, and repeated pip fetches across the 4-version matrix and across runs are measurable. Evidence from experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2 (P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE) shows adding actions/cache@v4 for ~/.cache/pip keyed on hashFiles('pyproject.toml') reduced measured CI time (~9.2%) while keeping the same install and test steps. I add a cache step after setup-python and before Install dependencies, sharding the cache key by matrix.python-version so parallel matrix jobs do not contend for one key and wheels are not restored across incompatible Python versions. All lint, pylint, pytest, and docs steps are preserved unchanged; no permissions, secrets, deployment, or new network access is added. fail-fast was not applied because the workflow explicitly requires outcomes for every Python matrix version.
